solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scot's pretty heartless, certainly not fed up!

indicators.note: losing the heart means the middle letter of the Scots word is taken away

parts.note: bonny is the Scottish word for pretty

explanation.surface: A Scot remarks that someone is not very pretty, and plainly not fed up with anything either.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' looks like 'fed up with'; read literally it means fattened, which a skinny person is not. 'heartless' drops the middle N.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skinny and angular has plainly not been fattened or well nourished.

clue.text: £50 in pocket, have fine attire

indicators.note: the two letters sit in the word for pocket, so the pocket holds them

parts.note: to pocket something is to bag it, and a bag is a pocket of sorts
L is the pound sign's letter (libra) and L is the Roman numeral fifty
to have something is to own it

explanation.surface: Someone pockets fifty pounds and treats themselves to smart clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The pound sign gives L (from Latin libra) and 50 gives L as a Roman numeral, so the £50 is two Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: A long formal dress worn to a dance is a prime example of fine attire.

clue.text: Just managed to put up with Lowry novel

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upward, so backwards

parts.note: to put a candidate forward is to run one, past tense ran

indicators.note: novel means new, so the painter's name is made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone barely tolerates a novel by Lowry, or about the painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses RAN to NAR, and 'novel' turns LOWRY into ROWLY.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something only just, by a small margin, is to manage it by a whisker.

clue.text: Two boys look embarrassed to get a big hand

parts.note: Roy and Al are two boys' names
to flush is to go red, looking embarrassed

explanation.surface: Two lads blush when they win a large round of applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big hand' suggests applause; here it is a hand of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ace to ten in one suit is the highest-ranking hand in poker, so a very big card hand.

clue.text: Round and large character

parts.note: a round shape looks like the letter O
mega means very large

explanation.surface: Someone is described as rotund and a big personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is a letter, here of the Greek alphabet, not a personality.
explanation.definitionFit: The final letter of the Greek alphabet is a written character.

clue.text: Saltire bedecked by a church's patterned covering

indicators.note: the cross is decorated on either side by the other letters, so it sits inside them

parts.note: a minster is a large church
a saltire is a diagonal cross, shaped like X

explanation.surface: A Scottish flag is adorned with a church's patterned cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The saltire is the St Andrew's cross on Scotland's flag, an X shape.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a kind of woven carpet, originally from a Devon town, with a pile and a pattern, covering a floor.

clue.text: Dossier's place in affair besetting current politicians

indicators.note: to beset is to surround, so the word for affair goes around the letter

parts.note: a fling is a brief love affair
I is the symbol for electric current
the cabinet is the senior group of government ministers

explanation.surface: A dossier turns up in a scandal surrounding today's politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'present-day', but it gives I, the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Office furniture with drawers for storing folders and documents is where a dossier is kept.

clue.text: In France, a key old international agency

parts.note: un is French for a
Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: In France, an old key belongs to an international body.
explanation.definitionFit: The United Nations' educational, scientific and cultural organisation is a worldwide agency.

clue.text: What about two media bigshots gets noticed

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the interjection is read backwards

parts.note: eh is an exclamation meaning what?

indicators.note: two means the abbreviation appears twice over

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a big figure in the media

explanation.surface: Someone asks what it takes for a pair of media moguls to get attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses EH to HE; 'two' doubles ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To take heed of something is to pay attention to it, so it was noticed.

clue.text: Endless fun with French girlfriend in US city

indicators.note: endless means the word for fun loses its final letter

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun
amie is French for a female friend

explanation.surface: A man has a fun but never-ending time with his French girlfriend in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts the K from LARK.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a city in Wyoming in the United States.

clue.text: Noticing Mafia criminal blowing things up

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notices the Mafia blowing things up with criminal intent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing things up' sounds like bombing; it means enlarging, as with a lens.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlarging an image, as a lens or photocopier does, is a way of making it bigger.

clue.text: Dramatist, English writer, penning story

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the writer's name goes around the other word

parts.note: Sir Thomas More was the English author of Utopia
a story can mean a lie, as in telling stories

explanation.surface: An English writer is busy writing a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'story' means a fib here.
explanation.definitionFit: The French comic playwright who wrote Tartuffe was a dramatist.

clue.text: Alcohol's taken in small drops — it's silky stuff

indicators.note: the word for alcohol takes in a letter, holding it inside

parts.note: grog is alcoholic drink, originally rum and water; the 's reads as has
rain falls as drops of water

explanation.surface: Liquor is sipped in tiny drops, smooth as silk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alcohol's' is read as 'alcohol has', so GROG has S taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a heavy ribbed silk or rayon fabric, used for ribbons, so a silky material.

clue.text: Med resort's inspiring hotel in suitable place

indicators.note: inspiring is read as breathing in, so the resort takes the letter inside

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Mediterranean coast
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean resort's hotel occupies a fitting spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' is read literally, breathing in.
explanation.definitionFit: A position that suits someone well is their own fitting place in life.

clue.text: Backing statute, rulers second support for motion

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for statute is read backwards

parts.note: a statute is a law
kings are rulers
a tick is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: Rulers back a statute and then second a motion in debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support for motion' suggests seconding a proposal; it means a cane for getting about.
explanation.definitionFit: A cane carried to steady oneself while walking supports a person's movement.

clue.text: Barge in front of canal has great horses around

indicators.note: to horse around is to fool about, so these letters are jumbled
the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A barge at the head of a canal has big horses standing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barge' looks like a boat; here 'barge in' is a verb. 'horses around' is the anagram signal, not the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive at a party uninvited is to push in where one is not wanted.

clue.text: Beastly male with an aggressor's weapon

parts.note: a tom is a male animal, especially a cat
a is the shorter form of an
a hawk is someone who favours aggressive policy

explanation.surface: A brutish man arms himself with an attacker's weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' means of a beast, not nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A light axe used by Native Americans was a fighting weapon.

clue.text: Agreed East End's in need of renovation

indicators.note: something needing renovation is to be rebuilt, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Officials agreed that London's East End needs doing up.
explanation.definitionFit: To give consent to a proposal is to go along with it.

clue.text: Pub riot, with cokes spilled? It's young people's entertainment

indicators.note: spilled drinks are scattered about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A pub brawl sees cokes spilled: is this fun for the youngsters?
explanation.definitionFit: Illustrated volumes for small children are a form of amusement for the young.

clue.text: Jumped in Sierra before accident

indicators.note: before puts the first letter ahead of the word for accident

parts.note: S is Sierra in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a prang is British slang for a minor car crash

explanation.surface: Someone leaped about in a Sierra car just before crashing it.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sierra was a Ford car, which suits the crash, but here it is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprang is the past tense of spring, to leap.

clue.text: Property to develop? Not at first

indicators.note: not at first means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: to gestate is to develop, as an embryo does in the womb

explanation.surface: Is this property ripe for development? Not at first.
explanation.definitionFit: A large piece of land with a house on it is landed property.

clue.text: High official and old men laugh

parts.note: old man is slang for father, and pa is short for father
ha is the sound of a laugh

explanation.surface: A senior official and some old men share a laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a high rank in the Ottoman Empire, given to governors and generals.

clue.text: Building feature: walls in Nevada and Delaware

parts.note: the punctuation mark in the clue is called a colon

indicators.note: the walls of a word are its outer letters

explanation.surface: An architectural feature: walls in two American states.
explanation.walkthrough: The punctuation mark itself gives COLON; the walls of Nevada and Delaware give NA and DE.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of columns supporting a roof or beam is an architectural element.

clue.text: Left port carrying cargo

parts.note: Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship left port with cargo on board.
explanation.definitionFit: A loaded vessel is heavy with a load, weighed down by goods.

clue.text: Tongue in need of a drink

parts.note: Arabic is a language, or tongue

explanation.surface: Someone's tongue is parched for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' is a language, not the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The bean from the main coffee species makes a cup of coffee, so a drink.

clue.text: Take away starter of tempura transported back

indicators.note: back means the whole string is read backwards
the starter of a word is its first letter

parts.note: carted means transported, as goods in a cart

explanation.surface: A takeaway's tempura starter is sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take away' suggests a meal; it means to reduce. 'back' reverses TCARTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish the worth of something is to subtract from it.

clue.text: Bird's places for putting some wool, say

parts.note: on a golf course, putting happens on the greens
a hank is a coiled length of yarn, such as wool

explanation.surface: A bird's chosen places for stashing some wool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' is golf putting, not placing.
explanation.definitionFit: A wading bird of the sandpiper family with green legs.

clue.text: Runner would briefly lose control in motion

parts.note: a ski is a runner, as on a sledge
would shortened is 'd, as in I'd

explanation.surface: A runner would quickly lose control while moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' is not an athlete but a ski.
explanation.definitionFit: To slide uncontrollably, as a car on ice does, is to lose grip while moving.
